terms.grammar: verb, irregular (prae + sum), with the dative
terms.gloss: be in charge of, head, run
evidence: Caes. BC 3.61: alicui negōtiō praeesse, to have charge of a business (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 1.6.1: omnibus negōtiīs nōn interfuit sōlum, sed praefuit
terms.comment: With the dative of what one is in charge of: quī oppidō praeerat (Caes. BG 2.6, Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative and the dative
terms.comment: aliquem reī praeficere: to put someone in charge of something.

phrases.latin: quae gerantur, accipiēs ex Polliōne, quī omnibus negōtiīs nōn interfuit sōlum, sed praefuit
phrases.english: what is going on you will hear from Pollio, who was not only involved in all the business but in charge of it

sources: Lewis & Short: praesum · Lewis & Short: praeficio
Cicero’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
